title: NFL Street → standalone Windows game
goal: Reconstruct the game in native code, with its own Windows runtime and locally supplied game assets. No Dolphin, ModernGekko, or ISO needed while playing.
current: The menu retains both selected lineups and field choice. Native checks load all 14 players’ geometry, textures and materials together and now bind selected face/hair models to fresh initialized skeleton sources transactionally. Original player draw submission matches the GPU calls. The scene still uses reference actors; body skinning, fresh actor/instance state and renderer execution remain open.
next: Join fresh body/skinning and skeleton-to-actor inputs, construct model instances and matrix palettes, then feed the verified player draw to the native renderer and running menu match recipient.
why: Every appearance input of a selected player is reproducible from disc data plus the menu's choices, and the exact GPU calls the game makes to draw a player are now known and reproduced natively. What remains for a visible selected player is running those calls in the native renderer with fresh actor state.
boundary: Daywater is the research workbench: it inspects the original game, captures behavior, and checks claims. NFL Street reconstruction and its eventual Windows runtime stay in the separate game project. The web interface organizes research; it is not the native game itself. Private game data, generated code, builds, and diagnostics stay on W:.

capabilities.title: Playable reference
capabilities.description: A Windows prototype reaches a match and accepts movement input, slowly. It still uses ModernGekko/Dolphin and the original game data.

capabilities.title: Verified native slices
capabilities.description: Score events, bounded player movement, and target-record handoffs replay in Windows C. Two players advance together from a RAM snapshot for three checked frames; four later handoffs match two fresh captures.

capabilities.title: Standalone game
capabilities.description: Native field/sky rendering and two controllable reference player instances, each with eight-direction movement, stops, restarts and animation. Experimental V changes supported player-1 sets. Original roster assembly, contacts, ball gameplay, fresh startup, audio and menus remain unfinished.

milestones.title: Establish a reproducible research reference
milestones.description: Use the original game as the comparison target so reconstructed code has something reliable to match.
milestones.evidence: Daywater reads documented score and selected-player position fields and traces live writers. The Windows reference reaches a saved match and accepts movement input.
milestones.acceptance: The research setup restores known states and produces reproducible observations for the identified game revision.
milestones.remaining: Every new state or game branch still needs its own evidence. This milestone establishes the workbench, not native gameplay.

milestones.title: Reconstruct useful game behavior in native code
milestones.description: Replace bounded pieces of original behavior with readable, independently executable code.
milestones.evidence: Native score replay reproduces failed and successful PAT events. Player input and movement outputs match recorded live calls, including direction changes and partial input strength. A two-player loop matches complete output blocks for three consecutive frames.
milestones.acceptance: The movement and scoring paths needed by a chosen match segment work across its input and state transitions and match fresh original-game captures.
milestones.remaining: Broader animation-dependent movement and target selection, other actor branches, collision, launch/catch/bounce scheduling and match rules. Eight-direction normal movement and braking are checked; ball plane sampling is checked in controlled calls. Verification covers identified saved states and branches.

milestones.title: Run a deterministic match segment without the emulator
milestones.description: Join reconstructed behavior into a simulation that owns its updates and carries game state forward.
milestones.evidence: The snapshot-start Windows executable matches three original-game frames for two actors. Timing matches 30 updates; stream setup and early-stage decisions match fresh captures. Native contact selection produces its own paired requests. The newer paired contact application now owns links, allocation, clip setup, callback metadata, transition decisions and completion: two fresh runs match both complete actor objects and the complete selection manager. Eight direct transition searches also match. These pieces are not yet a continuously running match segment. Native bank resolution now derives the tested source tables from twelve disc bank blocks. Two controlled original-game experiments verify successful spawning of different clips and match six full actor checkpoints and the duration per run.
milestones.acceptance: A longer segment advances all relevant actors, selection changes, and match events in the correct order from one initial state, with checkpoints matching fresh reference runs.
milestones.remaining: Join contact, timing, event processing and movement; establish actor eligibility and scheduling; expand naturally occurring transitions. Fresh match state and animation frame interpretation remain open. Independent DAT traversal and an owned bank catalog are now implemented.

milestones.title: Make the independent Windows game playable
milestones.description: Connect independently reconstructed game behavior to native Windows rendering and controls.
milestones.evidence: Native Windows field/sky rendering and two independently controlled reference players work with eight-direction starts, movement, braking and stops. Source clip selection, phase/rate updates, bounded four-channel fades and supported inspection set changes pass controlled original comparisons and Windows checks. Fixed source-backed contact inspection renders both finite streams and completes; natural contacts remain open. Ball state/release services match 867 original records, with 864 association joins and 1,728 time/XY samples. Compact hand posing matches 2,784 complete matrices and 192 wrist-position joins. Full actor attachment position/quaternion and corrected associated-ball outputs each match 576 controlled original cases across three saved contexts. Native orientation diagnostics run through contact and direction/set playback (806 and 2,118 calculations), retaining all 26 corresponding baseline captures. Existing NAP1 inspection remains compatible. These are bounded services and inspection gameplay; visible ball possession and full match startup remain unfinished. The subsequent complete attached update matches 576 full ball records and 576 visual-model poses, including velocity and scale; 806 contact and 2,118 direction/set native updates pass, with captures unchanged. Existing original draw evidence identifies shared GameBall geometry; visible fixed attachment is now connected. Original GameBall resources match two captures; 513 native triangles/UVs pass independent checks. 576 ordinary render bases match original float words. Actual Windows movement/contact checks render an animated wrist football, while all 26 ball-disabled captures and both player exports remain identical. Automatic possession and full gameplay remain open. Complete original assignment matches 576 full records, actor flags, context effects and model poses. Optional native ownership inspection switches the visible football between both animated players and releases/reassigns it; direction/set and paired contact runs each pass six assignments/two releases. Detached rendering freezes the last pose; no free-flight claim. Bounded complete airborne update matches 1,536 original records, including force integration, field limits, no-spin orientation and plane sampling. Optional Windows airborne mode passes movement/contact checks with 121/64 moving detached updates; all 12 prior ownership captures remain identical. Force/context inputs and ground-plane stopping are host choices; launch/collision policy remains open. The complete per-player draw submission (80161E10) is native: 854 original runs per saved context (14 captured players, 840 controlled variants) match every GX call with its arguments, the render state and all other RAM, in three contexts repeated twice. Executing it in the native renderer remains open.
milestones.acceptance: A player can start and finish a match in the independent Windows executable, with working gameplay, rendering, audio, and controls.
milestones.remaining: Independent actor creation, automatic gameplay animation-set eligibility, broader original transition choices and root travel and full callback context routing; join other actors and contact scheduling; ball launching/catching/bouncing and automatic ownership, appearance/camera/effects fidelity, fresh match initialization, rules, audio and menus. The native movement executor selects a bounded normal-context handoff; other original game-service branches remain open.

milestones.title: Verify, package, and broaden coverage
milestones.description: Turn the first playable native match into a dependable standalone build.
milestones.evidence: Current comparisons establish confidence only for the documented revision, states, and branches; they do not establish whole-game compatibility.
milestones.acceptance: Fresh native starts and complete matches pass repeatable checks, unsupported behavior is documented, and a Windows build runs with local assets and no emulator dependencies.
milestones.remaining: Broader modes and scenarios, performance, saves, controller coverage, build packaging, and regression checks against the original game.
